Title: Boulder City Council Study Session - July 27, 2023 (Police Oversight Ordinance Update; Use Table and Standards Update - Neighborhood Centers)
Overview: The Boulder City Council study session on July 27, 2023, covered two topics: a preliminary review of revisions to the city's police oversight ordinance, including panel scope, selection, onboarding, and training, and the third module of the use table update for neighborhood center business and mixed-use zones. Council members supported the police oversight work and asked for comparisons with other cities, and they broadly backed streamlining restaurant approvals and expanding small-business uses while debating ground-floor residential uses, drive-throughs and gas stations, and clubs and hostels. No formal decisions were made, and the police oversight recommendations are expected in the fall, while the neighborhood center ordinance is slated for October after community input closes July 31 and planning board review in August.

Topic1.Title: Police Oversight Ordinance Revision Update
Topic1.Summary: Consultant Farah Muscadin presented preliminary observations and community feedback on revising Boulder's police oversight ordinance, including panel scope, selection process, onboarding, and training. Council asked about whether issues stem from ordinance drafting or implementation, the meaning of oversight versus advisory roles, the monitor's non-voting role on the panel, and the use of outside counsel. Council members expressed support for the work and asked for comparisons with other cities. The work group timeline targets community feedback in late summer and recommendations in fall.

Topic2.Title: Use Table and Standards Update: Neighborhood Centers (Module 3)
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the third module of the use table project focused on neighborhood center business and mixed-use zones to implement comprehensive plan policies for walkable 15-minute neighborhoods. Proposed changes include easing restaurant approvals, allowing duplexes and townhomes on ground floors in BT and BR districts, reconsidering vehicle-related uses downtown, and allowing additional uses like retail, post offices, and small performance venues. Council broadly supported streamlining restaurant approvals and expanding small-business uses, with debate on residential ground-floor uses, drive-throughs and gas stations, and clubs and hostels. Community engagement via a story map and questionnaire closes July 31, with planning board review in August and an ordinance expected in October.
